experiment: Experiment 4 -- section-aware boost/filter by section_path type (T-DOC64)
verdict: STOPPED before implementation -- section_path is present but does not carry reliable Method/Results/Introduction-style semantic labels for the book corpus this experiment targets. No boost was built. No A/B eval was run.
method: Read-only measurement of rag/retriever.py's data model (Chunk.section_path / blocks.section_path) against papers.db (file:...?mode=ro), corpus-wide and restricted to the 5-book eval fixture's paper_ids, plus a keyword-based canonical-category classifier (method/results/introduction/discussion/conclusion/related_work/abstract/references/acknowledgments/appendix/limitations/other) applied to every non-empty section_path value found.

collection_chosen_for_the_would_be_AB_ru.name: exp1_ctrl_sizemerge_idf
collection_chosen_for_the_would_be_AB_ru.reason: Per the experiment brief: identical to production except IDF is on, the configuration this project is likely to ship. Verified read-only (not used, since the experiment stopped before the A/B stage).

noise_floor.passage_level: assumed same order pending contrary evidence, per experiment brief

corpus_wide.description: All 11,026 papers in papers.db (research papers + the 5 books), 361,614 chunks total.
corpus_wide.note: Field is NOT sparse (96.8% non-empty). Research papers follow IMRaD-ish conventions closely enough that a loose keyword classifier resolves 55.7% of non-empty values into a canonical category (method+results alone = 26.8%) -- this population, if it were the target of Experiment 4, would plausibly support a boost. It is not the target: the 40-question eval fixture this experiment must be measured against is 100% doc_type=book.

five_book_eval_corpus.description: The 5 books backing the 40-question eval fixture (fixtures/eval/eval_book_questions.json), 1,939 chunks total -- the actual population any Experiment 4 boost would act on for this eval.

local:dfe850b3281a.title: Causal Inference and Discovery in Python

local:54d6ca71dda9.title: Causal Inference and Machine Learning in Economics, Social, and Health Sciences

five_book_eval_corpus.note: Field is essentially never empty (99.6% non-empty), but 86.6% of non-empty values are DISTINCT -- section_path here is a free-text subsection heading (worked examples, 'Notes > 5.1 Bias-Variance Trade-off', single-letter appendix markers A-W, OCR-garbled math snippets used as headers e.g. '## Best lambda for Ridge regression: 0.2529632'), not a stable enumerable type taxonomy. Only 16.3% (method+results combined) resolve to a canonical IMRaD-style label under a deliberately generous keyword classifier; per-book method+results share ranges 6.4%-33.8%, itself too variable to calibrate one boost weight across the corpus.

eval_fixture_gold_labels.description: The 40-question fixture's own gold_chapter_title-adjacent section_path field (the fact-bearing block's actual section), categorized the same way -- i.e. what the boost would need to promote to matter for this eval.
eval_fixture_gold_labels.note: 70% (28/40) of the eval set's own gold answers sit in a section_path the classifier cannot map to Method/Results/Introduction at all -- a boost built on that taxonomy would have no effect on 7 in 10 questions, and could only help the other 3 in 10 if it never mis-scores the boundary. Separately: question_type is uniform ('Book-Chapter-Recall') across all 40 questions -- the plan's assumption that a Method/Results-seeking subset could be isolated via the harness's existing by_question_type breakdown does not hold for the fixture as actually authored; there is no tagged subset to test a targeted boost against without post-hoc relabeling questions after their retrieval-relevant content is already known, which the eval set's own authoring discipline (write-before-retrieval) exists specifically to avoid.

decision.criterion_applied: Experiment brief: 'If the field is too sparse or too inconsistent to support a boost, that is a legitimate and valuable finding -- report it and stop rather than building a boost over unusable data.'
decision.finding: section_path is not sparse for books (99.6% populated) but IS too inconsistent to support the specific Q4 hypothesis (favor Method/Results-shaped sections over Introduction-shaped ones): 80.4% of book chunks and 70% of the eval fixture's own gold answers fall outside any Method/Results/Introduction-style category, the field is instead a near-unique free-text subsection heading per chunk (86.6% distinct), and the eval fixture carries no question_type subset to even target the boost at.
decision.action_taken: Stopped at the read-only investigation stage. No boost implemented. No toggle added to rag/retriever.py. No A/B eval run against exp1_ctrl_sizemerge_idf or any other collection -- there is no 'no-boost arm' number to report because no boosted arm was built to compare it against.
decision.T-DOC64_status: Remains a documented idea without measured support, same status as before this experiment (per docs/METHODS-books-and-chunk-quality.md's own framing of the falsification criterion) -- this run adds the read-only section_path distribution as the reason, not a new open question.
